answer: Let trust propagate through the attestation graph by bounded-length random walks, so influence reaches a node only along supported paths. A sybil cluster connected to honest participants by a sparse cut has low conductance: few walk steps cross its boundary, limiting imported trust and the cluster’s aggregate voting weight. Min-cut bounds make this limit explicit; a meadow of mutually attesting identities cannot gain weight merely by echoing a sonnet across a narrow bridge.
